newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in sleepy trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in sleepy trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in sleepy late trading on Monday.
"It's a slow day. There is no drive at all," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding that sentiment was mixed in thin trading.
Dealers said rates were trapped in a narrow range between 2,429.0 and 2,430.0 throughout the day.
The U.S. bank dealer said there were some attempts to break the rupiah at the 2,430.0 level due to ample liquidity in the afternoon, but overall support remained strong.
Spot rupiah was at 2,429.0/29.5 at 0245 GMT, little changed from the opening level of 2,429.0/30.0.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,428.85/29.25 and 2,429.6/29.75, respectively.
Dealers said ample rupiah supply did not affect the spot value but softened longer-term swap rates. Overnight rupiah fell to six percent from 11.0/12.0 percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.1/0.2 and tom/next at 0.15/0.20.
The dealers said there seemed to be no worry in the market over weekly tax payments due Tuesday, reflected by relatively stable tom/next swap rates.
One dealer in Singapore said earlier foreign players were still maintaining long rupiah positions in the forward market.
He said many players were likely to overborrow the rupiah as long as the baht remains vulnerable to foreign attacks.

Dealers said a decision by the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) to put off acceptance of last month's general elections was not a factor in the market although people were watching out for possible statements.
One-month swaps declined to 11.0/12.0 from 11.5/12.0, two to 24.25/24.75 from 25.00/25.25, three to 37.0/38.5 from 38.0/38.5 and six to 76.0/77.0 from 77.5/78.5 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,419/2,611 and its conversion band at 2,419/2,467 on Monday.
